items.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I just did a tour with the singer Madeleine Peyroux, and opening for Sarah McLachlan

ctx.x: Well there’s certainly a lot of styles: Cajun music and things that are kind of surfacing.

Well there’s a lot of focus on the past just in general, in all kinds of music. I mean rock music now, pop music, I just did a tour with the singer Madeleine Peyroux, and opening for Sarah McLachlan who’s like a pop singer, and I got to know the musicians and the music, and I’ve kind of been away from that scene for a while. And it’s like musicians who play pop music basically study everything that’s happened in the past thirty or forty years and kind of synthesize things, sort of the way I’ve done with…
generation has to kind of destroy the music of the past and create a new kind of music. But the trouble is now they’ve sort of run out of things to do.
